claim: On the Megascale holdout, ProteinDPO reached Pearson R 0.72-0.73 for dDG correlation, above SFT (0.59) and vanilla ESM-IF1 (0.55)
quote: Although the SFT model modestly improves (Pearson R = 0.59, Spearman ρ = 0.57) from vanilla ESM-IF1 (Pearson R = 0.55, Spearman ρ = 0.53), ProteinDPO clearly surpasses both models (Pearson R = 0.72–0.73, Spearman ρ = 0.69–0.72)

claim: AUROC for classifying stabilizing vs destabilizing variants: vanilla 0.74, SFT 0.76, ProteinDPO 0.82-0.84
quote: observe the same trend in the vanilla (AUROC of 0.74), SFT (AUROC of 0.76) and ProteinDPO models (AUROC of 0.82–0.84)

claim: Every model scored multi-mutation variants worse (R 0.3-0.5) than single-site substitutions (0.5-0.8)
quote: We found that all models perform worse when scoring variants with multiple mutations (Pearson R and Spearman ρ = 0.3–0.5) (Fig. 2c) compared with their ability to score single-site substitutions (Pearson R and Spearman ρ = 0.5–0.8)

claim: Scored additively from single-mutation likelihoods, ProteinDPO underperforms ThermoMPNN (0.36-0.40 vs 0.41)
quote: ProteinDPO underperforms ThermoMPNN (ProteinDPO Pearson R = 0.36–0.40, ThermoMPNN Pearson R = 0.41)

claim: Scored by whole-sequence likelihood, all ProteinDPO models surpass ThermoMPNN on double mutations (0.44-0.48)
quote: However, when we use ProteinDPO to score variants by the likelihood summed across the whole sequence, all ProteinDPO models surpass ThermoMPNN (Pearson R = 0.44–0.48)

claim: ThermoMPNN's architecture and training restrict it to single mutations
quote: By contrast, the architecture and training procedure of ThermoMPNN restricts the model to single mutations.

claim: ProteinDPO is competitive with ThermoMPNN on S669 (0.44-0.47 vs 0.43) and FireProt (0.6 vs 0.65)
quote: (ProteinDPO Pearson R = 0.44–0.47, ThermoMPNN Pearson R = 0.43)

claim: On FireProt ProteinDPO reaches Pearson R 0.6 against ThermoMPNN's 0.65
quote: (ProteinDPO Pearson R = 0.6, ThermoMPNN Pearson R = 0.65)

claim: SFT improved on the Megascale holdout but fell slightly on FireProt (-0.05) and S669 (-0.01), evidence of overfitting; ProteinDPO's gains generalized (+0.13-0.16)
quote: does slightly worse on the FireProt (Pearson R decrease of 0.05, Spearman ρ decrease of 0.04) and S669 datasets (Pearson R decrease of 0.01), while the improvement of ProteinDPO over the Vanilla model generalizes to FireProt (Pearson R and Spearman ρ increases of 0.13–0.14) and S669 (Pearson R and Spearman ρ increases of 0.13–0.16) as well, evidence that the SFT model has overfit to the training data while ProteinDPO has incorporated generalizable stability information.

claim: On SKEMPIv2 protein-protein complexes ProteinDPO gained only 0.02-0.04 in Pearson/Spearman and 0.04-0.05 AUROC
quote: ProteinDPO has modestly increased scoring of the binding affinity of large protein–protein complexes (Pearson R increase of 0.02–0.04, Spearman ρ increase of 0.02–0.04 and AUROC increase of 0.04–0.05)

claim: Gains were larger on antibody-antigen complexes (AB-Bind): Pearson +0.04-0.08
quote: larger performance gains when scoring antibody–antigen complexes (Pearson R increase of 0.04–0.08, Spearman ρ increase of 0.03–0.10, AUROC increase of 0–0.02)

claim: The SFT model failed to generalize to binding-related tasks
quote: the SFT model fails to generalize to binding-related tasks.

claim: On 483 clinical and human-derived antibody melting points ProteinDPO improved on vanilla ESM-IF1 by 0.08-0.12
quote: ProteinDPO improves (Pearson R and Spearman ρ increases of 0.08–0.12) on the ability of vanilla ESM-IF1 in ranking the differences in

claim: Supervised Megascale dDG models such as ThermoMPNN cannot score multichain proteins or produce absolute stability values
quote: other supervised models trained on Megascale to predict ΔΔG (such as ThermoMPNN) cannot evaluate proteins with multiple chains (such as most antibodies) or produce absolute stability metrics.

claim: For backbones of 136-394 residues, ProteinDPO generations were predicted substantially more stable than vanilla, SFT and the native sequence
quote: sequences generated by ProteinDPO for much larger backbones (136–394 residues) are predicted to be substantially more stable (lower energy) than vanilla ESM-IF1, the SFT model and the native sequence.

claim: ProteinDPO generations had lower native-sequence similarity than SFT or vanilla yet confident ESMFold structures (pLDDT >80)
quote: despite having lower similarity to the native sequence than SFT and vanilla ESM-IF1, sequences generated by ProteinDPO have confident ESMFold-predicted structures (pLDDT >80)

claim: Six of the top-30 ProteinDPO substitutions exactly matched the eight stabilizing mutations reported in prior H1/H3 literature, with five more at identical positions
quote: among the top-30 substitutions tested, six (H26W, K51M, K51I, E103I, E103L and N95L)

claim: Baseline models recovered only one literature stabilizing mutation; ProteinDPO had a higher recovery rate at every top-n level
quote: While other models were able to recover one mutation, ProteinDPO has a higher recovery rate across all top-n levels.

claim: ProteinDPO zero-shot identified H26, K51 and E103, the hypothesized pH switch governing the post-fusion transition, over a >500-residue search space
quote: ProteinDPO successfully identified critical residues (H26, K51 and E103) which make up the ‘pH-switch’ hypothesized by Milder et al. to modulate the pH-sensitive transition to the post-fusion state

claim: The remaining HA mutations were mostly cavity-filling substitutions in the helical core introducing Leu, Trp, Tyr and Phe
quote: The remaining mutations primarily consist of cavity-filling substitutions in the helical core involving the introduction of leucine, tryptophan, tyrosine and phenylalanine residues that enhance hydrophobic core packing

claim: Of the top-30 single substitutions measured by DSF, 19 raised Tm by >1 C and 7 were within 1 C of wild type
quote: Of these, 19 variants obtained greater thermal stability (Tm) than the wild-type HA (>1 °C improvement), and 7 variants obtained similar melting temperature (<1 °C difference)

claim: Only the SFT and vanilla models placed any of the six strongly stabilizing (>=9 C) substitutions in their top 200
quote: Only the SFT and Vanilla models were able to recover mutations in their top 200

claim: No model could rank the 30 variants' Tm, but SFT and ThermoMPNN classified them as stabilizing/destabilizing at F1 >0.75 while missing the most stabilizing
quote: the SFT model and ThermoMPNN show strong ability (F1 score >0.75) to classify them as stabilizing or destabilizing (Extended Data Fig. 5), despite crucially failing to capture most highly stabilizing mutations

claim: All nine-substitution variants beat wild-type Tm, the best by up to 17 C
quote: all nine-substitution variants achieved greater thermal stability than the wild type, with the most successful variants achieving improvements of up to 17 °C

claim: The best nine-substitution variant did not significantly surpass the best single substitution, but nine-substitution variants averaged 9.8 C more stable
quote: While the best nine-substitution variant did not significantly surpass the best single-substitution variant, nine-substitution variants were 9.8 °C more stable on average than single-substitution variants.

claim: DPO-4, DPO-16 and DPO-19 raised Tm by 10 C (with a 32 C shift in the major transition), 17 C and 12 C
quote: with 10 °C (with a 32 °C change in the major thermal shift transition), 17 °C and 12 °C increases in Tm, respectively

claim: Nine-substitution variants retained nanomolar or subnanomolar affinity to head- and stem-targeting bnAbs despite mutations in or near the epitopes
quote: despite several mutations being located within or adjacent to key antibody-binding epitopes (Fig. 5a), we observed strong nanomolar or subnanomolar affinities for all antibody–antigen pairs

claim: CD spectra at 20 C and a melt to 95 C confirmed the variants kept the native HA's secondary structure character
quote: circular dichroism (CD) spectra at 20 °C and a melting profile up to 95 °C confirmed that variants preserved the secondary structure character of the native HA

claim: Transferred into 2024 Texas and British Columbia H5N1 strains, DPO-16 gave 13 C and 32 C Tm improvements
quote: DPO-16 achieves 13 °C and 32 °C improvements in Tm compared with native HA from the Texas and British Columbia strains, respectively

claim: 80% of ProteinDPO-identified variants increased or maintained stability, from only 45 total designs
quote: We observed that 80% of

claim: Testing only 45 total designs achieved up to 17 C Tm improvement
quote: Testing only 45 total designs, we achieved up to 17 °C improvements in melting temperature (Tm).

claim: Generalization across 20 years of viral evolution suggests ProteinDPO stabilizes by fundamental structural principles rather than strain-specific changes
quote: This suggests that ProteinDPO stabilization occurs via fundamental structural principles rather than strain-specific modifications.

claim: ProteinDPO has not clearly surpassed all supervised models at scoring, but RL alignment preserves generative capability that regression models cannot combine
quote: it has not clearly surpassed all supervised models in scoring25 (Fig. 2b,d,e). However, using RL, unlike supervised regression, preserves essential generative capabilities.

claim: Explicitly discouraging the post-fusion state was not considered in variant generation; further evidence is needed for vaccine-grade antigenic properties
quote: explicitly discouraging the postfusion state was not considered in variant generation but could be considered in future versions of our scoring procedure

claim: Megascale domains were Foldseek-clustered at 50% alignment and clusters assigned 90/5/5 to train/validation/test to prevent leakage across structures
quote: clusters were randomly assigned to respective train (90%), validation (5%) and test (5%) datasets to ensure generalizability of the model across different structures.

claim: All models were trained on absolute dG rather than relative ddG because more data points carried dG and loss/validation accuracy barely differed
quote: We found negligible difference in loss and validation accuracy training with either metric, so all models were trained on ΔG as more data points had ΔG measurements.

claim: A third, new DPO objective ('weighted') was derived that directly incorporates scalar labeled data
quote: we also derive a third, new DPO training objective (‘weighted’) that directly incorporates scalar labeled data

claim: Chain A (head) was excluded from the multi-site combination pool because ProteinDPO heavily preferred chain B (stem) substitutions
quote: we excluded chain A of hemagluttinin (head region) as defined by PDB 6CFG from the pool of single-site substitution variants, given ProteinDPO heavily preferred variants in chain B (stem region).

claim: Rosetta energy is acknowledged as potentially inaccurate and no substitute for experiment, used because it is physics-based rather than sharing ML training data
quote: Although Rosetta energy can be inaccurate and is not a substitute for experimental testing, it is a widely used independent evaluator of machine learning generations due to its reliance on physics-based parameters rather than shared training data with machine learning models

claim: Variant selection averaged percentile ranks across three H5N1 HA structures to reduce bias from any one experimental structure
quote: this procedure was repeated across two other available structures of H5N1 hemagluttinin (PDBs: 2FK0, 6CF5), and the percentile ranking of mutants within each structure were averaged.

claim: A gap level of 0.5 performed best on validation data for pair selection from scalar labels
quote: we found a gap level of 0.5 performed the best on validation data
